Toxic comment (but true): 99% of you will never come close to the level of actual top-tier C++ programmers. I say this from experience—I work directly with two of them, and trust me, the gap is enormous. Unless you started coding at 10 years old and never took a break, you’re simply too far behind. Real C++ work is a different universe from the stuff most people do. Writing a couple of scripts, sending HTTP requests, or wiring up some DevOps pipeline (or whatever you call "AI" now) doesn’t even scratch the surface. Most of you are just copy-pasting from Stack Overflow and pretending you understand what’s going on under the hood. Meanwhile, real C++ engineers are writing code that needs to run at the absolute limit of hardware, dealing with memory management, concurrency bugs, and performance bottlenecks you can’t even imagine. You can’t learn that from a bootcamp or some "learn to code in 30 days" YouTube playlist. The truth is harsh, but most of you will always be at the script kiddie level. That’s just the reality.
